title: StomachClear
question: How does the stomach digest food?
hook: Your stomach is a muscular bag of acid strong enough to dissolve meat, yet it doesn't digest itself. Swallow a bolus, cut the stomach open, watch it churn food into chyme three times a minute, and meet the germ a doctor drank to win a Nobel Prize.

explainer.title: A 25 cm tube and a J-shaped bag
explainer.text: Food goes from the mouth down the oesophagus, about 25 cm long, through the diaphragm into the stomach, which sits under the left ribs. The stomach has a fundus, a body, an antrum and a pylorus, a ring of muscle at the exit. Its wall has a folded lining and three layers of muscle.

explainer.title: Swallowing is a squeeze, not a slide
explainer.text: Chewing mixes food with saliva, whose amylase starts on starch. When you swallow, the epiglottis seals the windpipe for about a second, then a peristaltic wave carries the bolus down in about 5 to 10 seconds. It even works upside down.

explainer.title: Acid that doesn't burn its maker
explainer.text: Parietal cells use proton pumps to make hydrochloric acid, keeping the stomach at about pH 1.5 to 3.5. Chief cells make pepsinogen, which acid turns into pepsin to cut proteins. A mucus gel full of bicarbonate keeps the lining nearly neutral; weaken it and an ulcer can form.

explainer.title: A mill with a gatekeeper
explainer.text: About three times a minute a squeeze sweeps towards the pylorus, grinding food into chyme. The pylorus lets through only bits under about 1 to 2 mm and jets the rest back. Water leaves in minutes; a meal takes about 2 to 4 hours, and fatty food the longest.

explainer.title: Hungry, full and growling
explainer.text: The empty stomach holds about 75 mL but relaxes to take 1 to 1.5 litres. Stretch receptors signal fullness up the vagus nerve, ghrelin rises before meals, and gastrin calls for more acid. Growls are gas and fluid being squeezed along.

explainer.title: When things go wrong
explainer.text: Acid slipping past a weak sphincter causes heartburn. Most ulcers are caused by the germ H. pylori, which Barry Marshall proved by drinking it in 1984; spicy food doesn't cause them. Vomiting is a protective reflex run by the brainstem. For your own health, talk to a doctor.

concepts.def: The 25 cm muscular food pipe from the throat to the stomach.
Waves of muscle squeezing that push food along the gut.
The ring of muscle that lets food into the stomach and keeps acid out of the oesophagus.
A stomach cell that makes hydrochloric acid using proton pumps (H⁺/K⁺-ATPase).
An enzyme, activated by acid, that breaks proteins into smaller pieces.
A gel laced with bicarbonate that protects the stomach lining from its own acid.
The soupy mix of partly digested food and gastric juice that leaves the stomach.
The stomach's exit, whose sphincter lets through only small particles.
The hunger hormone, made mostly by the stomach, which rises before meals.
